i0: Modal verbs help us ask for things, offer help and ask for permission **politely**: ***Could** you help me? **May** I come in? **Shall** I carry that for you?*
i1: In English, how polite you sound depends a lot on the words you choose. This page goes from simple requests to very polite and formal ones.
rop-requests.t: Can you…? Could you…? Asking someone to do something
rop-requests.s: **Can you…?** and **Could you…?** + base verb ask someone to do something. *Could* is more polite: *Could you close the door, please?*
rop-requests.b1: To ask **someone to do** something, use *Can / Could / Would you* + base verb: ***Could** you **speak** more slowly, please?*
rop-requests.b2: To ask **for something**, use ***Can I have…?*** or ***Could I have…?***: ***Can I have** a glass of water, please?*
rop-requests.b3: Add ***please*** to sound more polite. Common answers: *Sure. / Of course. / No problem. / Sorry, I can't.*
rop-permission.t: Can I…? Could I…? May I…? Asking for permission
rop-permission.s: **Can I…?** (informal), **Could I…?** (polite) and **May I…?** (formal) ask for permission: *May I come in?*
rop-permission.b1: ***May I…?*** is the most formal. It's common in shops, offices and with people you don't know well.
rop-permission.b2: To **give** permission, use *can* or *may* (not *could*): *Yes, you **can**.* / *You **may** go now.* (formal)
rop-permission.b3: Don't answer *Could I…?* with *Yes, you could*. Say *Yes, you **can**.* or *Of course.*
rop-permission.w1: Give permission with can, not could.
rop-offers-suggestions.t: Offers and suggestions: Shall I…? Shall we…? Would you like…?
rop-offers-suggestions.s: Offers: **Shall I…? / Can I…? / I'll…** Suggestions: **Shall we…? / Let's… / Why don't we…?** Invitations: **Would you like…?**
rop-offers-suggestions.b0.0.1: ***Shall I** open the window? **Can I** help you? **I'll** carry that.*
rop-offers-suggestions.b0.2.1: ***Shall we** go out tonight? **Let's** take a taxi. **Why don't we** eat here?*
rop-offers-suggestions.b0.3.1: ***Would you like to** come to dinner?*
rop-offers-suggestions.b1: ***Shall I / shall we*** + base verb is used for offers and suggestions, mostly in British English: ***Shall I** call a taxi?* In American English, people often say ***Should I…?*** or ***Do you want me to…?***
rop-offers-suggestions.b2: ***I'll*** + base verb makes an offer at the moment of speaking: *You look busy. **I'll** make dinner.*
rop-offers-suggestions.b3: *Let's* + base verb (no *to*): ***Let's go*** (not *Let's to go*). Negative: ***Let's not*** argue.
rop-would-you-mind.t: Would you mind…? Do you mind if…?
rop-would-you-mind.s: **Would you mind + -ing?** = a polite request. **Do you mind if I + present / Would you mind if I + past** = asking for permission. Answer *No, not at all* to say yes!
rop-would-you-mind.b0.1.2: ***Do you mind if I sit** here?*
rop-would-you-mind.b0.2.2: ***Would you mind if I opened** the window?*
rop-would-you-mind.b1: *Mind* means *object to* (not like). So the polite answer **yes** is ***No, not at all*** / ***No, go ahead*** / ***Of course not***: *Do you mind if I sit here? ~ **No, not at all.*** (= Yes, you can.)
rop-would-you-mind.b2: If you do mind, say something like: *Actually, I'd rather you didn't. / Sorry, that seat is taken.*
rop-would-you-mind.w1: No = I don't mind = you can.
rop-allowed.t: Be allowed to: permission and rules
rop-allowed.s: **be allowed to + verb** = have permission: *We **are allowed to** use phones at break.* Past: **was allowed to** / **could** (general). Rules: **not allowed to**.
rop-allowed.b0: ***Be allowed to*** describes permission given by someone else or by a rule: *Students **are allowed to** use dictionaries in the exam. You**'re not allowed to** smoke here.*
rop-allowed.b1: It works in all tenses: *Will we **be allowed to** take photos? I **wasn't allowed to** go out late when I was a teenager.*
rop-allowed.b2: For **general** permission in the past, *could* is also possible: *When I was a child, I **could** stay up late at weekends.* For **one particular** occasion, use ***was allowed to***: *I **was allowed to** leave early yesterday.* (not *I could leave early yesterday* for a single permitted action)
q.rop-would-you-mind-s02: *Do you mind if I use your phone?* Which answer means *yes, you can*?
x.rop-would-you-mind-s03: *Would you mind if I* + past simple.
